episodes.210964: Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through the area near a semi-stationary front across central and east-central Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening on Monday (4/13).  The strongest storms produced hail up to 2 inches in diameter.  ||Repeated rounds of showers and thunderstorms from Monday afternoon (4/13) through early Tuesday morning (4/14) caused Flash Flooding as 2 to 4.5 inches of rain fell across central and east-central Wisconsin.
episodes.210972: Supercell thunderstorms developed along and east of a dryline across east central Kansas late afternoon on April 13th.  The storms produced very large hail to the size of baseballs and also a strong tornado in Franklin County and a brief weak tornado in Osage County.  3 injuries were reported due to the Franklin County tornado none serious.
episodes.211297: A dryline set up over easternmost portions of MAF's CWA. Pulses in the southwesterly flow aloft once again encouraged the development of a couple of thunderstorms in the Permian Basin and Big Bend/Lower Trans-Pecos. One storm managed to become severe, producing large hail (quarter to ping-pong ball sized) in Mitchell County.
episodes.211374: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of east central Illinois during the afternoon of April 13th, producing isolated hail and localized wind damage.
episodes.211375: Scattered thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Indiana during the afternoon of April 13th, producing isolated hail and localized severe wind gusts.
episodes.211783: Severe storms moved into Wabasha County during the evening hours, bringing large hail to Lake City and resulting in numerous instances of hail damage in this area with 2 inch diameter hail being common in northern Wabasha County. Additionally, severe storms across southern Minnesota congealed into a line and pushed eastward into much of the rest of southeast Minnesota, bringing large hail and damaging wind gusts to the region.
episodes.211784: Severe storms moved into west-central Wisconsin from southeast Minnesota and brought large hail up to 3 inches in diameter to the area. Additionally, an EF-0 tornado occurred near Gilman, Wisconsin which was widely observed by spotters and the public. Some isolated wind damage occurred as well later into the evening as storms congealed into a line and pushed eastward.
episodes.212465: A southward moving cold front tracked across central and southern MN early Monday morning before stalling near Redwood Falls, MN over to Eau Claire, WI. Morning stratus associated with this frontal boundary aided an increased thermal gradient along this boundary. Later in the afternoon, a surface low centered over eastern Nebraska advected unstable air into much of southern MN. This airmass converged on the pre-existing stationary boundary which led to the initiation of several severe thunderstorms. Many thunderstorms produced large to very large hail measuring as large as 3.5 in diameter as well as four tornadoes across southern Minnesota.
episodes.212825: The combination of an approaching front, a developing pre-frontal trough, and a mid-to upper-level trough promoted a moist and unstable weather pattern across the |region. This resulted in flooding, landslides, flash flooding and hail from April 12th to 15th.
episodes.212916: A severe storm tracked across Chase County the afternoon of April 13th and produced up to baseball size hail.
episodes.212999: Thunderstorms moved across lower Michigan late on April 13th into the early morning hours of April 14th.  Large hail was common with limited damaging winds. Moderate to heavy rain occurred along with some localized inconvenient flooding with one to three inches of rain.
episodes.213104: A southward moving cold front tracked across central MN and northwest WI early Monday morning before stalling near Redwood Falls, MN over to Eau Claire, WI. Morning stratus associated with this frontal boundary aided an increased thermal gradient along this boundary. Later in the afternoon, a surface low centered over eastern Nebraska advected unstable air into much of southern MN west-central WI. This airmass converged on the pre-existing stationary boundary which led to the initiation of several severe thunderstorms across west-central WI. A few thunderstorms produced large hail measuring as large as 1.25 in diameter as well as localized flash flooding in southern Eau Claire County.
episodes.213110: At late afternoon, considerable moisture focused near a strong warm front from low pressure across northeastern Nebraska through northwest Iowa.  Climatologically significant mid-level lapse rates produced a strong capping inversion which gradually weakened north of the warm front. Storms initiated with effective deep-layer shear from 40 to 50 knots and quickly became severe hail producers north of the warm front across southeast South Dakota into southwest Minnesota during the late afternoon, with additional storms developing in proximity to the surface wave across northwest Iowa. One of these latter storms produced two weak tornadoes across northwest Iowa.

episodes.213128: Heavy rainfall and snowmelt resulted in flooding across the south-central U.P.  Many roads were flooded and several closed.  The flooding also caused damage at the Escanaba Airport (KESC) due to standing water on the runways and power failure. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th for Menominee and Marquette counties.
episodes.213151: There were a few rounds of thunderstorms through this period. A few storms were severe with large hail and damaging winds and an isolated tornado.
episodes.213204: A complex system brought severe winds to much of northern UT with a brief tornado along the border of Cache and Rich counties. Later on, this system would result in a flash flood event across southern UT.
episodes.213344: One severe thunderstorm developed and produced damaging wind gusts in Crook County.
episodes.213394: A mid-April low pressure storm system transitioning over the region brought additional amounts of rainfall, mainly to the mountains of Orange and San Diego counties.

Emergency management reported that the road into the Otter Lake Dam was completely submerged by 10 AM on the 18th. Trained spotters reported that the access to the wire weight gauge on the Sturgeon River at Chassell was impossible due to water over Sturgeon River Road. Damage was considered minimal and damage estimates are not available.

Emergency management reported multiple rivers and low lying areas were inundated by the combination of rain and snowmelt. In Gwinn, multiple roadways were inaccessible due to flooding on the Escanaba River by the 18th. Division Street in Negaunee was closed daily from the 13th onwards. Harlow Lake Rd (County Road HD) was closed at County Road 550 on the 17th. Flooding at Pelissier Lake in Sands Township resulted in 1 evacuation with well water being unsafe due to the high water table making septic systems inoperable. Ely, Humboldt, Champion, and Republic townships experienced water over multiple roadways, including the road at Steel Bridge Rd (Ely Township, County Road CG) on the 18th. The Chocolay River Fishing pier was underwater by the 19th. The Iron Ore Heritage Trail west of Wawanowin Rd to the city of Republic had flowing water on the trail by the 21st. 10 properties along the Michigamme River were inaccessible on the 23rd. Jasper Street in Ishpeming had a sinkhole that was filled on the 23rd. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th.

The tornado moved into Blue Earth County from Watonwan County. Based on multiple storm chaser videos, ground contact was evident most of the way, but not always, as there were two or three occasions when ground circulation was not evident for one or two minutes. But some storm chaser video showed it to be entirely from the same parent circulation, hence one tornado.  The tornado hit several farms.  At one farm, both garage doors on either side of a house were buckled in, multiple trees were snapped or large branches broken.  Two farm outbuildings had their garage doors blown out.  Some shingles were also removed.  Dozens of trees nearby were blown over. A small trailer was blown over 100 yards.  Another farm had two small outbuildings that were destroyed and trees down or broken.  The maximum wind speed was estimated at 90 mph.  This was based on drone video and ground-based photos provided by the Blue Earth County Sheriff's Office.
